note: The plates of the place (assets-src/venus/place/lay.py lays the close image back, assets-src/venus/place/build.py makes the full plates). Centre: aheadDeg of arc ahead of the point under the twin of place.json, along its heading. North at the top. Levels a, b and c each have half the half tangent of their parent; the widest, w, is 40 deg so the ground near the point under the camera stays inside the plates down to the height where level a alone covers the frame (G13 at frames 1296 to 1304); the deepest is a little wider than half so it holds the bottom of the frame at the twin. feather and fade are read by the globe shader like those of the patch pyramid; rim is the share of the half width over which the widest level fades out, measured on a circle.
lightNote: Memory (gate G15, at most 1400 MB for the full set): a plate of 4096 with all its channels counts 89.5 MB, one channel 22.4 MB. A level with `colour` holds its light alone in one channel and takes its colour from the plate of the level named there, which covers it. The channel is the light of the level (luminance, weights 0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722) over the light of that plate at the same ground point, not a display value, with `most` at the top of the range; the film shows that plate times the channel. So the forms of every level are held at full size, the colour of a, b and d at 1 in 1.7, 3.4 and 1.8 of it, and where a level is seen far smaller than it is held the picture goes to its colour plate, which is filtered in light as before (a channel of display values lost the small bright tops there: at 16 texels to a pixel 1.2 display values in the mean against 0.4 this way). Measured on the plates as 8 bit display values, the picture put together from the files against the full plate: assets-src/venus/place/tlay.py split, numbers in assets-src/venus/RECIPE.md.

wide.note: The wide ring (level v, assets-src/venus/place/wide.py): the forms of the place carried on round level w, a plate about the same centre, one channel. It is drawn only as forms over the globe's own colour (tone.live) and never as it is, so it holds no colour and no tone of its own. rim: the share of the half width over which it eases out, from the inscribed circle inward; formsDeg: the border follows its own cloud forms, drawn inward by up to forms (share of the plate width) where the plate is brighter at the first scale than at the second (degrees of arc at the centre). own: how much of the globe's own fine cloud forms stays under the ring (0: the ring lies on the globe's smoothed colour alone, so the globe's swirls dissolve as the ring comes in; 1: on the globe as it is, which showed hairlines between the towers; at 0.5 the lit cells of the globe stay in place from 1272 to 1283 and from 1588 to 1596 while the towers come and go, seen on native crops).

canvas.note: The source canvas: the 2x upscale of the approved close image at `at` with size `frame`, and below fullFromY the margins of the relief over the whole width (relief-L0 and relief-L1 of the full set, see RECIPE.md).

show.note: One ground for every height (MAIL 785, MAIL 815 point 5 b). The plates stand on the globe in every segment, and nothing of them goes by the height of the camera or by the clock; they arrive by the distance of the eye from the ground (far). The forms of the ground by their size on the ground: over tone.live.sigmaDeg they are the globe's own everywhere; between sigmaDeg and tone.live.sigmaDeg they are the globe's own outside the disc of the place and the plates' inside it (discDeg: degrees of arc from the centre of the plates, whole inside the first angle, ended by the second); under sigmaDeg they are the plates', and they take the place of the globe's own of that size by distance: none where a pixel of the master frame is wider on the ground than pixelDeg[1], all where it is narrower than pixelDeg[0] (degrees of arc, eased in the logarithm), so the exchange runs while those forms are a few pixels wide. The share by the line of sight (tone) moves the tone at tone.live.sigmaDeg alone, from the globe's to the plates', and no form. far (MAIL 981 point 2, MAIL 1001 point 1): the place arrives by distance. None of it stands where the shorter side of a pixel of the master frame on the ground is over far.pixelDeg[1] (degrees of arc), all of it where that side is under far.pixelDeg[0], eased in the logarithm: the plates and the wide ring are weighed by it, and where it is none the ground is the globe's own alone. The master frame is 1920 by 1080. At the hold the shorter side of a master pixel on the ground is about 0.10 to 0.12 degrees over the plates (worked out from the pose), so the hold is the approved globe's and holds nothing of the place (1185 and 1259 at draft equal to the tree of 8adf0940 to the byte); the place is whole where the eye is nearer than about two thirds of the hold's distance to the ground point. The shorter side goes with the distance of the eye from the ground point alone (the longer one grows with a grazing line of sight too). No height of the camera and no clock is read. While the place arrives its forms between the two sizes stand as cloud of the globe's deck does at that size: at the contrast far.contrast and within far.most times the colour under them, in full when it has arrived and in full by the share of the line of sight of T (tone). The colour under them is the globe's own as it stands in the frame, and where the look of the hold stands it is that look (globe.ts, under). discDeg was [4.5, 6.0] in the first state: beyond 6 degrees the frame of T (it reaches about 11.5 degrees from the foot of the eye) changed its forms of that size in place as the line of sight left the one of T.

texelsNote: Decision d253 (MAIL 802). What an exchange counts is the full set's texels in both sets, so the asset set does not move the moment at which a patch or a plate arrives or the place of a border: the web set is only softer. texels: the width of each picture in the full set (patches: the dive patches in their order; plates: the levels by tag; wide: the wide ring). The wrap and the pictures of the ground have theirs in wrap.json (color.full) and relief.json (imageSize.full). A mip level named in this file (forms.look, ground.matte.level) is a level of the full set's picture; the web set reads the level that covers the same ground. In the full set a picture of another width than the one written here stops the load.

forms.note: The border of the widest plate (level w) follows its own cloud forms and not a circle: the weight falls over rim (share of the plate width, from the inscribed circle inward), and the circle is drawn inward by up to look[0] of the plate width where the plate is brighter than its surroundings (the ratio of its mip levels look[1] and look[2]).

tone.note: The look of the place from above. The plates hold the tones of the close view at T: the far deck pale under its haze, the near towers dark against the Sun. Those tones belong to the line of sight of T. Seen from another direction the place is a region of the globe's cloud deck: there the plates give their forms alone, over the globe's own colour as it is lit in that frame (live). The plates show as they are stored by a share that is 1 at T. cos, curve: the share by the cosine of the angle between the line of sight at a ground point and the line of sight of the camera at T, none below cos[0], full above cos[1], the ramp between to the power curve. air: the share is multiplied by the ratio of the sine of the elevation of the camera at T above that ground point to the sine of the elevation of the camera now, not above 1, to this power: the air on a line of sight goes with one over that sine, so the pale haze of the far deck comes in as the camera sinks to the height of T and not while it still stands steep over that deck. near (MAIL 981, point 2): the share is also multiplied by the ratio of the distance of the camera at T from that ground point to the distance of the camera now, not above 1 and whole within 1 / 0.95 of T's distance, to this power. Seen along the line of sight of T from far off a ground point has the tone of the globe and not the one of the close view: without it the hold showed a dark hole of about 12 px at pixel 1360, 432, where its line of sight is the one of T. This reads the distance of the camera from the ground point; it moves a tone and no form, is 1 at T and falls steadily with that distance. The cause it stands in for is the air between the eye and the ground (MAIL 1001 point 2): from far off the tones of the close view lie under more air; the air's own law is to carry it later. No height of the camera is read (MAIL 815, 5b): until 25 Nov the share was also none above 0.6 radii and unchanged below 0.1 (heights); stills with that law out of reach differ from the ones with it by a mean of at most 0.61 of 255 (frames 1308 and 1560), the same picture by eye, so the angle and the air carry the share alone. Until the commit before this one a map per handover (place3-tone-dive.bin, place3-tone-rise.bin, made by tlay.py tone) carried a fixed power and factor instead of live; it gave a dark olive field about the place wherever the globe is lit otherwise than in the one view the map was fitted to, and is taken out.

dusk.note: The exposure of the globe side on the way to the place: the globe is drawn gain times brighter and turned by tint at the place, against the hold (the plates hold the light of the close image, which is exposed for dusk). Gain and tint rise in the logarithm as the camera comes down between the two heights (radii over the cloud tops, eased in the logarithm of the height): none above the upper one, all below the lower one, the same curve in the dive and in the rise and no clock in it. The upper height lies under the height of the first frame of the dive and of the last frames of the rise, so the hold and the travel are not touched. The plates are drawn at the same exposure and with the same share of the tint, so they are dim like the dusk about them when they come in and keep the colour of the globe about them at every exposure.
dusk.heightsNote: Before, the gain ran on the clock: over the shares 0.1 to 0.5 of the dive (frames 1269 to 1305, heights 2.9 to 0.21) and 0.5 to 0.9 of the rise (frames 1567 to 1597, heights 0.17 to 3.6). At the judged frames the share is nearly the same as before: 1287 0.505 (was 0.510), 1586 0.309 (was 0.316).
dusk.hueNote: Drawn dimmer than they are held, the plates take their colour from their display value and not from their light, by hue times the share by which they are dimmer: the light of a highlight that the film curve pressed has far more colour than the picture shows, and dimmed it turned the lit sides of the towers red. At the handover the plates are not dimmed and show as they are.
dusk.limbNote: The glow of the limb is a fit of the hold picture seen from far away. It is not raised by the gain. In the dive and the rise it is read for the eye of the far end of the move (the first frame of the dive, the end of the rise), held in the frame of the ground (set.ts, limbHeld; globe.ts and rim.ts, uLimbEye): it lies on the ground that eye sees at its limb, goes over the horizon with that ground on the way down and comes over it on the way up. Beside the body it has the share of its light that the ground at the live limb holds. No height and no angle of the live view sets its weight, so it does not slide over the cloud tops as a band. Before, it went out between two heights (limbHeights 0.5 to 1.6) and the pattern of the picture changed in place there: 0.83 at frame 1284 and 0.81 at 1575 against 0.45.
dusk.rampNote: When the gain ran on the clock the shares were first 0.2 to 0.6 and 0.4 to 0.8. With them the mean level of the body fell from 115 at frame 1260 to 52 at 1290 before the gain had risen, and came back to 83 at 1314; in the rise 85 at 1560, 50 at 1578, 98 at 1601. The place field was dark mud in the judged frames 1287 and 1586. The gain was then made to rise earlier in the dive and fall later in the rise, so the place is exposed while it is still small; the heights above keep that.

leave.note: The look of the hold (the lightning, the far limb, the rim of the hold) goes out as the camera comes down between these two heights (radii, eased in the logarithm): all of it above the upper one, none below the lower one. The upper height lies under the height of the last frame of the hold. After the surface view it stays out: the rise and the travel start without it, as before. Before, it went out on the clock over the first half second of the dive (frames 1260 to 1275, heights 3.46 to 1.92).

ground.note: The ground of the surface view on the globe side (relief.ts, updateGround): the meshes of the surface view and its air under the horizon hang in the globe's scene by the similarity of the plan, so the handover changes nothing in the picture. They have their full share below the lower height and none above the upper one (radii over the cloud tops, eased in the logarithm). The lower height lies above the height of both handovers (0.0208 and 0.0184). Above the upper height the place is the plates alone.
ground.trueNote: Where the ground is drawn (relief.ts): the picture of the surface view lies on its meshes as the surface view's own camera saw it; from another eye a part of it is drawn larger than it was seen. true: the ground has its full share where the smaller scale of that picture against the frame is at least the second value (1 from the surface view's own camera), and none under the first; there the plates show. It is taken for a face in the deck, and above the deck (tall, units of the surface view's scene over the deck sphere, the camera of the surface view stands 1 over it) for a face turned to the surface view's camera. skin: the same scale measured on each face of the mesh; under it the faces from a tower's top to the deck behind it are left out. All by angle and distance alone.
ground.releaseNote: At T the globe side has to be the surface view itself, which draws every part of its picture, also the parts another eye sees larger than they were stored. So inside the frame of T (frustum, below) true and skin are let go by the height of the camera over the height of T (a ratio, eased in the logarithm): in full above the second value, gone at the first. Between them both limits are multiplied by the same share, so the ground reaches by height into the parts it left to the plates. Measured without it on the merged tree: the two sides at T differed by a mean of 1.054 in the dive and 5.409 in the rise.
ground.keepNote: The near ground keeps all of its picture at every height: where the camera of T sees a point of the ground from above, at a sine of its elevation over the second value, true and skin never hold, inside the frame of T and outside it; under the first value they hold as before (by release inside the frame of T, in full outside it). It is the part of the ground that keeps its relief (flat, below). Before, true and skin came back over it between 1 and 3 times the height of T: the lit crests of the near towers went out by height while the flat plate stood there (rise 1547 to 1549, the pattern number 1.15), and outside the frame of T the near ground left by the angle of the eye (rise 1541 to 1551 at the left edge).
ground.matteNote: The border of the ground: the outline of its layers in the close image (left, right, lower edge) is three planes through the camera of the surface view. Toward them the ground gives way to the plates over width (units of the surface view's scene, by the distance from the nearest plane), sooner where its picture is dark and later where it is bright (forms: how far its own cloud forms move the border, share of the width; level: the level of the picture the forms are read at; scale: times the display value). The border stands still in space: it does not move by the height of the camera. Inside the frame of T (frustum, below) there is none.
ground.frustumNote: The frame of T: the camera of the handover with its field, as it stands in the scene of the surface view (set.ts, camAtT). Inside it the globe side has to be the surface view itself, so there the ground has no border and true and skin are let go by release. Outside it nothing is let go and nothing moves by height: the border stands where the matte puts it, and the ground is left to the plates where the camera of T sees it at a low angle, since from above that far deck is drawn larger than it was stored. margin: how far outside the frame of T, in half frames, the ground still counts as inside in full and from where on not at all. wide: the same outer limit for the ground near the camera of T (near), which gives way over this wider margin, so the edge of the frame of T does not show on it as a line. near: the sine of the elevation of the camera of T over a point of the ground under which the ground outside the frame is gone and over which it is whole. forms: how far its own cloud forms move that limit and the margin, share of each.
ground.flatNote: Where the ground lies flat on the deck (relief.ts, uFlat): the plates under the ground hold the picture of T laid on the deck along the lines of sight of T, and where the camera of T sees the deck at a low angle the ground gives way to them as the eye moves. There each point of the ground lies where the plates have it, on the line of sight of T through it, so what gives way and what takes its place are one picture in one place and from T nothing moves. sinElevation: the sine of the elevation of the camera of T over the point of landing under which the ground lies flat and over which it keeps its relief. horizon: the same sine under which it keeps its relief again, since a line of sight near the horizon of T lands far behind the tower it passes through.
ground.toneNote: The tones of the ground from above, by the law of the plates (tone, above): its stored tones belong to the line of sight of T and show by the same share as the plates' (cos, curve, air, heights of tone). Seen from elsewhere the ground gives its forms alone (its light over its own light at a coarse scale, broad, in widths of the image of the surface view; contrast, colour and most of tone.live) over the globe's colour at the place. under: that colour in scene light as the globe shows it at the place below the lower height of dusk.heights, measured from frames drawn without the ground (assets-src/venus/place/flay.py under); above that height it follows the exposure of dusk.
ground.bandHeightsNote: The air under the horizon (bandDeg) is the air as the surface view sees it from the deck. It comes in by the height of the camera between these two heights (radii, eased in the logarithm): none above the upper one, all of it at the height of the handover.
ground.layNote: The tones of the plates under and beside the ground (assets-src/venus/place/flay.py): the plates hold the picture of the surface view laid flat and show in the globe's light, the ground shows in the light of the place, so the plates take the broad tone of the ground. heights: the heights of the camera (radii over the cloud tops) at which the globe side is drawn with the ground and without it. grid: the size of the grid the tone ratio is worked out on, per level. edge: feather inside the border of the frame, share of the frame height. coverSinElevation: from where on a ground point counts (sine of the elevation of the camera over it). differs: the least difference of the two layer views, of 1, that counts as ground. insidePx: how far inside the drawn ground a pixel must lie to count, pixels of a frame 1080 high. sigmaDeg: the scale at which tones are compared, degrees of arc on the globe. reachDeg: the distance past the border of the ground over which the change fades out, degrees of arc. fade: the weights of the softened ground between which the change goes from none to all. ratio: the limits of a tone ratio. differPx: the scale at which flay.py differ compares tones, pixels of a frame 1080 high.
ground.bandNote: The air under the horizon is kept from the horizon down to the first angle (degrees under the horizon) and gives way to the plates by the second: the far deck fades into it, nearer by the ground covers it.

sky.note: The engine's sky on the globe side of the dive and the rise, by the height of the camera and not by the clock (plan.ts: skyShare, skyCarryShare, skyLiftAt). low: the sky of the surface view has its full share below the lower height and none above the upper one (eased in the logarithm); the lower height lies above the height of both handovers (0.0208 and 0.0184), so at the handover the sky is the surface view's. carry: how far the sky has turned from the globe view's frame to the surface view's, eased the same way between its two heights. lift: in the rise the stars open from the lower height up to the height the rise ends at. Before, the three ran on the clock: low over 24 frames before and after the handover (heights 0.075 to 0.021 and 0.019 to 0.16), carry over the whole move to the handover, lift from the handover to the end of the rise.

trust.note: Where the laid back picture is used as it is: inside the source canvas by edge (share of the frame height) and where the camera of the close image stands at least this high over the ground point (sine of the elevation, from no trust to full trust). Outside it the plate is repainted. soft: the border of that part is drawn in and softened by this share of the plate width. fine: source pixels for one plate pixel along the direction the laying back stretches most, from none to all of the laid back picture staying as it is; below it the picture keeps its place and its tones and takes its detail from the tiles.

air.note: The air of the place on the globe side (relief.ts: the dome of the close side, drawn from the globe camera, so it lies on the globe's own limb). Its weight is the field of the place (field, below). By its weight it hides the engine's Sun as the close side does, and the lens darkening is undone on the globe as on the close side.
air.fieldNote: MAIL 815, point 5 (a): the air is one field of the place and not a law by the heights above. It lies over the ground about the foot of the camera of T (the point of the cloud tops under it): whole inside the first angle from that foot (degrees at the centre of the body) and gone at the second, eased. The dome takes it at the ground point of its line of sight, or at the limb point under that line where the line passes over the limb, so the air stands whole over its place from the limb upward; the ground takes it at the ground point and by the line of sight to it (haze, below). top: over this cosine of the angle between the line of sight and the vertical at the ground point the line of sight is too steep to show any air, so the place seen from far above (the first frame of the dive, the last of the rise) holds none. Nothing of the air reads the height of the camera any more; heights (above) is left for the lens darkening alone, which is a grade over the whole frame. The limb point straight ahead lies at these angles from the foot (out/work/venus/place/airfield.ts): dive 23.1 at 1311, 19.3 at 1317, 16.2 at 1323, 14.0 at 1329, 11.8 at 1341; rise 12.4 at 1542, 15.2 at 1548, 19.7 at 1554, 26.7 at 1560.
air.hazeNote: The same air between the camera and the far ground: where the line of sight meets the cloud tops at a low angle the ground goes to the colour the close side has on its far deck at that bearing (the deck colours of the relief, look.ts). Weight: most times e to the minus (cosine of the angle between the line of sight and the vertical at the ground point) over mu, less its value at field.top and stretched to 1 again, times the field at the ground point. gain: the deck colour times this.
air.hazeMuNote: mu was 0.06. From 1547 to 1552 the eye stands over the horizon of T: the ground beyond that horizon is seen at a sine of the elevation of about 0.14 and took 0.09 of the far deck colour, so the globe stood there in its own orange brown as a second rim over the pale horizon the picture of T holds. At 0.12 it takes 0.28 there and 0.9 at the horizon as before: one pale band at 1547 (trials at 0.12 and 0.2 against 0.06, 17:30 to 17:38). The ground of the surface view does not take this law, so its last strip under the horizon of T stays as a darker patch of about 110 by 20 px at 1550, under the Sun.
air.hazeFieldNote: MAIL 815, point 5 (a): mu is 0.06 again, the value of the build b0b87889. At 0.12 the far deck of the place went pale from frame 1318 of the dive, since at a cosine of 0.15 to 0.3 the ground still took 0.26 to 0.07 of the far deck colour and that colour is mixed in scene light, where it is many times the ground. Seen at full size at 1320 and 1326 beside b0b87889 (stills of 00:31 UTC, 25 Nov): at 0.06 the far deck keeps its dark forms as there. With the first angle of the field at 13 and the second at 22 degrees the dome comes in at the limb as it did by the heights (0.16 at 1317, 0.48 at 1320, 0.92 at 1326, whole from 1332). What this gives back: in the rise the ground beyond the horizon of T stands in the globe's own orange brown over the pale horizon from 1547 to 1552 (hazeMuNote), as it does in b0b87889. Its cure is picture of the place beyond that horizon (the asset step), not a longer reach of the haze.
air.hazeBackNote: From commit 28d713f6 to a7f38721 this air had heights of its own (0.035 to 0.4 radii, mu 0.1). That made the pop number of the dive green (1.31 to 1.18) and laid a broad pale band along the limb at frames 1311 to 1323 of the dive and 1551 to 1560 of the rise, which washed the far towers; seen at full size beside the build b0b87889, main and the state before it (MAIL 788). It is taken back: the air goes with the heights of the dome again (air.heights) and mu is 0.12, the pop number is named as red.
air.sunNote: The Sun's own light in the air picture, and the rest of it (assets-src/venus/place/airsun.py, files relief-air-sun.png and relief-air-limb.png). The dome of the globe side lays the rest from the limb upward and the Sun's light from the limb as it stood at T, so the Sun keeps its direction when the camera climbs and the limb sinks, and at T the dome is the close side's own. atDeg: azimuth and elevation over the horizon of the Sun in the air picture (measured by the tool, which stops if they differ). boxDeg: what the Sun's picture holds about the Sun: azimuth to each side, elevation below, elevation above. halfWidthDeg: azimuth to each side of the Sun inside which light above the row's own level counts as the Sun's. smoothPx, rowMedian: smoothing along the row and median over rows before that level is taken. coreDeg: across the Sun the level is a blend of its two sides over this azimuth. edge: feather at the sides, share of the half width. rimDeg, rimHalfWidthDeg: below this elevation over the horizon the glow stays with the limb, and only this far to each side of the Sun the level is a straight line between the two ends. turnDeg: from the Sun down to this far below it the light blends into the light above the Sun turned half round. heights: the Sun's light is full below the first height of the globe camera (unit radii) and gone above the second, eased in the logarithm; between them the Sun and its glow are out of frame in both moves (the glow comes in at the top of the frame at about 1311 in the dive, height 0.135, and has left it by about 1564 in the rise, height 0.147).

sun.exactNote: The two files are a smooth split and their sum is not the air picture just over the limb beside the Sun (up to 18 of 255 at T, where the Sun's part holds its halo made whole). Below the lower height the rest is taken exactly, as the whole air picture less the Sun's part read from the limb as it stands now, so at T the dome of the globe side is the dome of the surface view; above the upper height it is the smooth rest of the file, and the Sun has left the limb by then. Radii, eased in the logarithm.
sun.exactCoreNote: In the Sun's core the air picture and the Sun's part both stand at the top of their range and their difference is rounding (it showed as coloured specks under the Sun once it had moved against the limb, at 1545 and 1547). So inside a window about the Sun nothing is taken as a difference of the two: the rest stays the smooth rest, and the Sun's light is the whole air picture read through the limb as it stood at T, less the smooth rest there, which is the read the close side makes. exactCoreDeg: the window is whole inside the first angle from the Sun and gone at the second (degrees of azimuth and elevation in the air picture; the Sun's part is over 0.95 of its range inside about 3.7 degrees and under 0.8 beyond about 7.5). exactUnderDeg: under the limb as it stood at T the air picture holds nothing; the window closes over this angle below that limb and the Sun's file stands there. With one window on both parts the sum at T is the air picture itself at every weight of the window.

atT.note: The plates at the T of a handover (assets-src/venus/place/tlay.py, files place3-<tag>-dive.jpg and place3-<tag>-rise.jpg, with -light before the kind for the levels that hold their light alone): the close side drawn at T is laid back through the globe camera of T. tags: the levels that are made again for each handover. edge: feather inside the border of the frame, share of the frame height. trustSinElevation: from where on the laid back picture replaces the plate (sine of the elevation of the camera at T over the ground point). coverSinElevation: from where on the plate takes the tones of the picture. soft: softening of the border of the replaced part, share of the plate width. toneSigma: the scale at which tones are compared, share of the plate width, by level (finer on the wide levels, which the frame at T sees at a low angle: there the plate keeps only its finest forms and takes the rest from the picture). ratio and floor: limits of a tone ratio and the level added to both of its sides (of 1). shiftDeg: the globe draws its plates this far (degrees of arc, east and north in the plate) from where the camera of tcam.ts alone puts them; measured by tlay.py calib on level d from the draw of the globe at T laid back against the plate it shows (with the shift the left over is under 0.1 plate pixels), cause not found.

build.note: Values of assets-src/venus/place/build.py. views: the check renders of the globe from straight above the plate centre with the plates off and the full dusk gain (check.ts --tops), from which the plates take the look of the globe at their rim. toGlobeDeg: arc from the plate centre over which the painted part goes from the tones of the close image to the tones of the globe.

takes.note: The tile takes kept for every level (top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right). 0: no tile take, the composition as it is.

edgeMatch.note: How a child plate is nested into its parent (build.py nest). ramp: share of the child's half width, from its border inward, over which its tones go from the tones of the parent outside it to its own. clip: limits of that gain. seam: where, in shares of the half width from the border, the child's own picture begins (outside it the child shows the parent's picture, enlarged); forms: how far the child's own cloud forms (sizes between formsSigma, shares of the plate width) move that line.

globeForms.note: Levels whose painted part is led by the globe's own cloud forms: the light and dark of the globe's look (forms between fromDeg and sigmaDeg of arc), limited to clip (floor: another lower limit for one level) and raised to power, laid on the carried colour of the close image in the guide. The plate then comes in over the forms it shows. Level b has a higher floor: a straight wind streak of the globe that passes the place came out of the tiles as a smooth dark trench with a hard line in it.
